title: Slide a flush cutting board to the counter-edge overhang, lift it level and rack it
instruction: Slide the cutting board from the butcher block to the counter-edge overhang, lift it level from below, and place it flat inside the dishwashing rack.
context: Every closing shift, prep cooks and dishwashers in commercial kitchens slide heavy flat cutting boards off the butcher block or prep table to the counter edge so their fingers can reach underneath and lift the board level into a dishwashing rack (US BLS OEWS occupations 35-2021 food preparation workers and 35-9021 dishwashers). A board lying flush has no grip until an edge hangs free in air, and pushing it past its halfway balance point tips it off the block, so the skill is stopping inside the safe overhang window, pinching the exposed edges and lifting level.
setup: Station table, both YAM arms parked at the back edge. A fixed reversible maple butcher block, 508 x 381 x 57.2 mm and 9.07 kg, sits centred at (0.320, +0.3405) m: its top face is at 804.7 mm and its -Y front face at y = +0.150 m is the counter edge the board slides over. The cutting board is a 457.2 x 304.8 x 12.7 mm white HDPE polyethylene board, 1.47 kg, a single free rigid body lying flush flat on the block top at (0.320, +0.3224) m, so its -Y edge sits at +0.170 m, only 20 mm back from the cliff and nothing yet hangs over. A fixed soft-gray polypropylene dishwashing rack, 502 x 502 x 101.6 mm and 1.43 kg, stands at (0.635, -0.395) m: a 19 mm floor plate and 6 mm walls leave an open inner cavity (x in [390, 880] mm, y in [-640, -150] mm) whose floor top is at 766.5 mm. The board is loose -- nothing welds or joints it to the block -- and the contact pairs are HDPE on maple at mu = 0.20 and board on polypropylene at mu = 0.40.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial. 1.0 if the board is completely inside the dishwashing rack's inner cavity, flat within 6 deg with its underside seated on the rack floor (between 8 mm below and 12 mm above the floor top), at rest, and both grippers are at least 40 mm clear of it. 0.5 if the board is upright within 10 deg with its -Y edge slid more than 30 mm past the butcher block's counter edge while it still lies over the block's span, or it has been lifted clear of the block, both grippers at least 40 mm clear, and it is not yet seated flat inside the rack. 0.0 if the board tips past 15 deg; or drops onto the table outside the rack (underside below table top + 12 mm); or tilts past 6 deg inside the rack or past 10 deg anywhere; or rides the rack walls without reaching the floor; or stays flush on the block (its -Y edge under 30 mm past the counter edge); or either gripper is within 40 mm of it. Possible scores: 0.0, 0.5, 1.0.
reset_notes: Set the cutting board flush flat on the butcher block at its start mark, empty the rack, and send both arms to ready pose.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (PhysX, 20 Hz). The cutting board is a single free rigid body; the butcher block and the dishwashing rack are fixed compound bodies built from boxes (a floor plate plus four walls; rack pegs and floor texture are not modelled). PhysX friction pairs use the cited HDPE-on-maple coefficient mu = 0.20 and rack polypropylene mu = 0.40; the slide and both edge pinches come only from the finger pads. Board flex and bevelled edges are not modelled.
